Vendor profile

Graebert

Graebert GmbH — German Developer of the ARES CAD Engine (Commander, Kudo, Touch) & OEM Licensing Partner

By GstarCAD Academy Engineering Editorial Board (Suzhou Gstarsoft Co., Ltd.) Reviewed by GstarCAD Academy Editorial Team Last reviewed 2026-10-26 Editorial Process & Testbed

1. Berlin Engineering Roots & the OEM White-Label Business Model

Founded in 1977 in Berlin, Germany by Wilfried Graebert Originally as an AutoCAD distributor and vertical plugin developer (FelixCAD, SiteMaster), Graebert GmbH pivoted in the 2000s to build its own cross-platform DWG engine: the ARES Trinity Ecosystem (ARES Commander for Windows/macOS/Linux, ARES Kudo for browser cloud CAD, and ARES Touch for mobile). Rather than focusing solely on direct retail sales, Graebert acts as the underlying OEM engine provider for Dassault Systèmes (DraftSight), CorelCAD, and Onshape Drawings.

2. Technical Architecture: ODA Teigha Foundation vs. GstarCAD Independent Kernel

While ARES Commander provides cross-OS compatibility, enterprise CAD managers evaluating ARES against GstarCAD 2027 must account for fundamental architectural differences in command syntax and plugin APIs:

  • Internal Command Naming Divergence: Like DraftSight, the ARES engine uses proprietary internal command strings (e.g., MAKEBLOCK, EDITANNOTATION, SMARTLEADER) and aliases them to AutoCAD shortcuts. Complex enterprise scripts or macro toolbars that invoke native AutoCAD command options frequently require manual refactoring in ARES, whereas GstarCAD maintains 1:1 native command and prompt parity.
  • C++ ObjectARX Porting Depth: GstarCAD's GRX SDK mirrors Autodesk's ObjectARX class hierarchy and memory management directly, enabling heavy C++ commercial plugins in civil, surveying, and electrical verticals to run with significantly higher stability and multi-core graphic speed on large 500MB+ DWG drawings.

5. Enterprise Co-Existence, Migration & TCO Optimization Protocol

In production supply chains where upstream 3D models or BIM containers originate from Graebert GmbH (Berlin, Germany) platforms, engineering IT directors optimize total cost of ownership (TCO) by deploying a tiered seat architecture centered on GstarCAD 2027 and DWG FastView:

  • Verified Data Exchange Pipeline: Migrate from ARES Commander or OEM clones to GstarCAD 2027 to gain 100% native AutoCAD command-name parity (no verbose MAKEBLOCK/SMARTDIMENSION translation) and superior GRX C++ plugin speed.
  • Eliminating Redundant Seat Rentals: Rather than purchasing high-cost authoring subscriptions for project managers, site engineers, estimators, CNC operators, and quality inspectors who primarily review geometry or annotate 2D DWG/DXF sheets, organizations equip 70%–80% of their workforce with GstarCAD Perpetual Floating Licenses (GstarLM) and FastView 3D.
  • Automated Database Hygiene Before Transmittal: Prior to archiving project deliverables or importing external vendor DWG exports into corporate PDM/CDE vaults, run GstarCAD's batch script sequence (-PURGE RegApps → OVERKILL → AUDIT Yes → INDEXCTL = 3) to guarantee sub-second opening times and zero proxy object corruption.
